task: What a solver that can only find, a stochastic local search, costs on the GF(2) encodings against kissat on the same file.
reading: A finds-only solver never refutes: its 'unknown' is the third answer and never a no. Its cost is a distribution over seeds, reported as every seed, the count finished within the cap, and the median where more than half finished. kissat is the fastest of three deterministic runs.

fixtures_provenance.conditions: Three solver processes at once on a 12-thread i5-12450H; CPU package between 84 and 95 C, touching the 95 C throttle point twice; clock 2.3 GHz on average when read; for part of the sweep another session's model runner at about half a core. So a second here is an order of magnitude, never a two-digit ratio.
fixtures_provenance.not_taken: kissat is unknown at the 60 s cap on cyclic_f2_7 at 13, f2_5x5 at 14 and matmul_3x3x3 at 23, both orderings. A rerun of those six cells at a 300 s cap was queued and killed with the challenge sweep before it ran; the cells stand at 60 s.

challenges_provenance.what_this_is: A five-second, one-seed smoke of the driver on the ten challenge-1 instances, run by hand to check the command before the full sweep. It is not the reproduction of Nawrocki et al.'s Table 1 and must not be read as one.
challenges_provenance.the_full_run: Five seeds for xnfsat and yalsat, one for the controls and kissat, 300 s cap, three jobs: started 11:19, stopped by hand at 12:16 on its third instance of ten (MM-23-2-2-2-2-B) after the chassis reached 96 C three times, with the two 300 s control rows per instance most of the load. Its partial results were not written; the command to run it unattended is in how-it-was-measured.md.
